sample_rows.title: Abrasive wheels and cut-off saws
sample_rows.points:
Only trained and authorised people may fit or change abrasive wheels and discs.
Check the disc is right for the tool and the material, undamaged and in date, and that its maximum speed is higher than the tool’s speed.
Use reinforced discs only on handheld machines. Set the guard to expose as little of the disc as possible.
Don’t force the disc, and never grind with the side of a cutting disc.
Wear eye, hearing and respiratory protection. Use water suppression or extraction when cutting masonry or concrete.
Watch where the sparks go. Protect other people and combustibles, and work under a hot works permit where required.
Isolate the tool before changing a disc, and never put it down while the disc is still spinning.
Ask the team: what checks do you make before fitting a new disc?

sample_rows.title: Accident prevention
sample_rows.points:
Most accidents come from people not thinking, cutting corners or ignoring their instructions and training.
Never remove guards, barriers or signs, and never use faulty equipment or make improvised repairs.
Only use plant, machines and products you are trained and authorised for. Check the CoSHH assessment before using any product.
Keep the work area tidy: no tools left where they can fall, no trailing leads, clean up as you go.
Never point compressed air at yourself or anyone else, and no horseplay on site.
If you see something unsafe, stop and report it to the site manager. Make it safe if you can do so without risk.
An injury can cost you your income, your hobbies and time with your family. Think about who relies on you.
Ask the team: what would you do if you saw an unsafe condition on this job?

sample_rows.title: Alcohol, drugs and medication
sample_rows.points:
Alcohol and drugs slow your reactions and affect judgement, balance and vision. On site that gets people hurt.
Nobody works under the influence. Anyone unfit for work will be stood down, and CBS policy may lead to disciplinary action.
Alcohol takes time to leave your body, roughly one unit an hour. A heavy night can leave you unfit to work or over the drink-drive limit the next morning.
Some prescription and over-the-counter medicines cause drowsiness. Tell your supervisor if you are taking anything that could affect you.
If you are worried about a workmate, tell the site manager. It could save their life.
If you have a problem, talk to us. Confidential help is available, for example FRANK on 0300 123 6600. We would rather help than lose you.
Ask the team: what would you do if a workmate turned up unfit for work?
